dedupe_keys.name: bosco limite forested infiltration area for managed aquifer recharge veneto italy

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes Bosco Limite in Carmignano di Brenta, Veneto, Italy, a forested infiltration area that recharges the unconfined aquifer of the upper Veneto and Friuli plains, which supplies most of the drinking water of both regions. River water is diverted through infiltration channels in a newly planted oak and hornbeam forest, a design first developed in 2007 by Veneto Agricoltura, with the aim of saving about 12,000 cubic metres of water a year while adding biodiversity, landscape and ecosystem service benefits. The infiltration system, with sediment control and monitoring of infiltrating water, was built from 2011 to 2013 with funding from the LIFE+ project AQUOR (2011 to 2015, total budget about 1.8 million euro) and the forest with regional funds. The page is free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal (2018), with sources from Veneto Agricoltura, Etifor and the Brenta Land Reclamation Board. Caveats: it is one site, measured recharge and quality gains are reported by the project, and the approach needs highly permeable soils. It illustrates green infrastructure for groundwater supply resilience to drought; a related record is the Oppla nature-based solutions repository.
name: Bosco Limite forested infiltration area for managed aquifer recharge (Veneto, Italy)
outcomes: A forested infiltration area built from 2011 to 2013 recharges the regional aquifer with a target of about 12,000 cubic metres of water saved per year, alongside biodiversity and landscape gains.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study on Veneto Agricoltura, Etifor and the Brenta Land Reclamation Board
